annotation.title_clean: Greening the Machine Question: Towards an Ecological Framework for Assessing Robot Rights
annotation.title_en: Greening the Machine Question: Towards an Ecological Framework for Assessing Robot Rights
annotation.authors_or_issuer: IOS Press (Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 335)
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Abstract page for a paper in the IOS Press volume on culturally sustainable social robotics. It proposes an ecological, materialist framework for assessing when robots may be eligible for rights, drawing on the growing legal recognition of rights of nature and other nonhuman entities.
key_provisions_or_claims: Presents an ecological framework for evaluating conditions under which robots may be eligible for rights
Argues a critical, materialist, ecological reading of environment supports extending rights to nonhuman entities
Draws on jurists' decisions establishing rights of nature as support
Notes robots are increasingly human-like and legal systems increasingly recognize nonhuman rights
